blockMcqs.question: What is the golden rule of performance engineering?
options: Optimize the cleverest-looking code first
Measure where time goes before optimizing
Add caching everywhere by default
Rewrite the hottest function in C
blockMcqs.explanation: Intuition about hot spots is usually wrong; profiling reveals the real cost.

blockMcqs.question: Why do latency-sensitive systems keep utilization below ~80%?
options: Above 80% the CPU physically overheats
Throughput drops sharply past 80%
Queues form near full, so latency spikes
Errors become impossible to log
blockMcqs.explanation: As utilization nears 100%, queueing makes wait time climb toward infinity.

blockMcqs.question: On a flame graph, what does a box's width represent?
options: When in time the function ran
Total time in that function and its children
How many times the function was called
The function's source-code line count
blockMcqs.explanation: The x-axis is total time, not a timeline; the widest leaf is the hot path.

blockMcqs.question: A part is 5% of runtime. Amdahl's law caps total speedup near:
options: Unbounded if you optimize enough
blockMcqs.explanation: Even infinite speedup of a 5% slice can only remove that 5% of total time.

blockMcqs.question: Why does a slow tail matter so much in fan-out systems?
options: Fan-out lowers the average latency
Waiting on the slowest of many calls dominates
Tail requests are retried automatically
Percentiles are cheaper to compute than means
blockMcqs.explanation: With 100 calls, rare per-backend slowness almost always hits at least one.

blockMcqs.question: Which fix usually gives the largest performance payoff?
options: Reducing object allocations
Connection pooling
A better algorithm or data structure
Adding async parallelism
blockMcqs.explanation: Changing the big-O wins orders of magnitude; the others are constant factors.

blockMcqs.question: What is the N+1 query problem?
options: Running one query that returns N+1 rows
One query per item instead of one batched query
Querying a table indexed N+1 times
A query that retries N times then fails once
blockMcqs.explanation: Invisible on small data, explosive on large; fix with an IN clause or join.

blockMcqs.question: Why can a microbenchmark report a function taking 0 nanoseconds?
options: The function was inlined into the caller
Compiler deleted code whose result is unused
The clock resolution was too coarse
Sampling missed the function entirely
blockMcqs.explanation: Dead-code elimination removes work with no observed output; consume the result.
